_comment: Every colour, timing and size knob in the UI lives here. Nothing visual is hard-coded in a component. Edit this file, reload, done.

palette._comment: Each section's own colour, named once: a tab, a grammar role, a unit. Tab, role, pos, unit, science and the tones all point here as "@name". No look repaints these: a look's tone (themes.tone) works each one out for its own ground, keeping the hue so a section is recognisable in every look, setting lightness and chroma, then darkening or lightening until it reads (lib/tone.js). Each is written as --palette-<name>; a token that points at one is written as var(--palette-<name>), so it follows a look switch on the page, not only at build.

color._comment: The default look, Ink: the landing page's warm black and gold, so the app and the welcome page are one place. Gold is the brand accent (primary); on-accent is what is written on a filled accent (the ground on a dark look, the card on paper). The other palette hues stay for roles and tabs.

unit._comment: Colloquial unit cards cycle through these; a unit's number picks one, so the same unit keeps its colour.

world._comment: Grow world colours (worlds.json ids). colorFor('world', id).

grow._comment: Grow's worlds. backdrop-opacity is how strongly a world's faded picture (components/grow/Backdrop.jsx) shows through under its content: kept faint so the map and the cards stay the point. gold is what is learnt and won: a finished lesson's star, the medal, a run of right answers; the light look has its own, since its amber is deepened for text and reads brown as a fill.

sky._comment: Grow's Night Sky (components/grow/scenes/Sky.jsx): dark navy in every look, since it is a night, not a surface. bg and edge the card, line joins the known stars, text its caption; star-on a known ayah, star-learning one met but not known yet, star-off one not met.

tab._comment: default is what an unknown id wears, the primary purple, so colorFor('tab', id) is the one rule for tab colour everywhere.

similar._comment: Similar verses (components/similar): the asked verse and its twin, each in its own colour wherever either is named or marked.

science._comment: Card colour of each map science (shell/MapPanel), keyed by chart id. One hue each, all readable on the raised surface, borrowed from the tab palette.

space._comment: Gaps shared across tabs. panel is the gap between the blocks of every tab, header included (the .panel class). card and tile are the insides of .card and .tile.

layer._comment: The one stacking scale: every z-index in the app is one of these, never a bare number. Lowest first: raised lifts a piece over its neighbours, seal is the Quran backdrop, below the page so results sit over it, backdrop is the drifting-lights canvas, below even the seal, sticky is a bar that pins while scrolling, popover a floating panel opened from a button, header the app bar, overlay a full-screen sheet, tip a tooltip over everything.

backdrop._comment: The faint seal behind a tab (quran/QuranSeal). ink is its colour, strength how much of it shows (wide: once a search fills the page); a light theme changes these two only.

lights._comment: The lantern backdrop: soft out-of-focus lights drifting slowly on a dark warm ground, behind every tab. count is how many lights, size-min-px and size-max-px how wide the smallest and largest are, speed how far one drifts per frame at motion.scale 1 (so the Animations setting slows it, and 0 stops it), alpha how bright a light is at its middle. tint is the share of lights that wear the tab's own colour instead of one of the warm lights, so the tab changes the room without painting it. Kept faint on purpose: the words on top are the point, and lights that compete with them are a distraction rather than a mood. ground-top and ground-bottom are the dark the lights float on. colors is the warm lights, comma separated, that the rest of the lights are drawn from. blend is how a light meets the ground: lighter adds glow to a dark ground, multiply stains a light one.

marks._comment: Large faint Arabic letters drawn on the backdrop canvas under the lights, in the tab's colour, so the page reads as Arabic before a word is on it. count is how many (0 draws none), size-min-rem and size-max-rem the range of letter heights, alpha how visible each is (kept far below the lights so the words on the glass stay the point), drift-px how far a letter wanders from where it sits (0 holds it still; speed is the backdrop's, so the Animations setting slows it), letters the pool drawn from, repeats welcome, and font the face, which must be the one the app already loads for Arabic.

glass._comment: The frosted pane the page content sits on, so the lights behind it read as a soft glow rather than as noise under the words. blur-px is how far the lights are smeared, alpha how much of the surface colour covers them (100% would hide them).

tabstrip._comment: How much of its own colour an unselected tab keeps. 0% is plain grey, 100% is as loud as the selected one.

timeline._comment: The timelines tab: acc-s and acc-l are the saturation and lightness every section hue is drawn at (its accent), ink-l the lightness of text in that hue; then the map's two grounds. Every section wears the tab's own colour, so the Seerah and the unseen sections read as one design.

cursor-light._comment: The cursor light: one faint circle that follows the pointer on every tab, tinted by the tab's own colour, so the page points at what is being read without a word of instruction. size-px is how wide it reaches, white how much of the page's text colour (white on dark, ink on light) sits in the middle, and tint how much of the tab's colour bleeds out from it. Small and faint on purpose: at full strength it reads as a torch and the text under it stops being the point. The Animations setting turns it off with everything else.

tamreen._comment: The two underline colours on a Tamreen picture question: blue for a possible حال, green for a possible ذو الحال. Their own group, not 'role', because they mark a candidate in the picture rather than a settled grammatical role.

mic._comment: The capsule microphone, the mark that means dictation: capsule, three grille slits, cradle arc, stem. weight is the stroke on the mark's own 24-grid, so it scales with wherever it is drawn. pulse-ms is one beat of the grille level-meter while recording; hover-pulse-ms is that same beat run slowly on hover, a preview of what pressing does. chase-ms is one lap of the arc's chasing dash while thinking.

lexicon._comment: The shelf of classical dictionaries under a root. entry-h is how much of an entry is shown before the rest is folded behind Show all: Taj al-Arus on أمر is 23,000 letters, and printed whole one book would bury the three under it. Enough to tell whether this is the entry wanted, not enough to be a wall. In rem, so a browser's own text setting moves it with the words. reading-w is the widest a line of English in a book runs: across a wide screen Lane's lines ran past a hundred letters and the eye lost its place going back to the next.

daleel._comment: Daleel's passage cards. passage-h is how much of a passage shows before the rest folds behind Show all: one fold for the whole card, Arabic and English together, in rem so it is about three lines of the Arabic it quotes however small the English beside it is. Counted in the English's lines it cut the Arabic to one line on a phone.

command._comment: The command line: the bar in the header and the orbit launcher behind the pen. rest-w is how wide the bar sits when nobody is using it and open-w how wide it grows on focus, both in rem, so a longer placeholder needs a number changed here and not a class edited. orbit-r is the radius the seven tabs sit at in the launcher, sat-w the width of one of them, and rail-w the strip of letters beside a result list. hint is the keys line under the launcher's ring, which sits straight on the modal's scrim rather than on a card: quiet on a dark scrim, but a light look's scrim is a mid grey that only full ink reads on.

wheel._comment: Every dropdown is ui/WheelPicker. type-from is how many choices a list needs before its card shows a box to type in; a shorter list is quicker to spin. loop-from is how many a list needs before it spins round, last choice above the first; fewer than the five rows on show would see itself twice.

dance._comment: How a group of things arrives: each one small and gathered at the middle, then springing out to where it belongs, one after another. Written as its own group rather than inside the launcher because it is the .dance class in styles/motion.css, which anything can wear: a ring of tabs, a row of cards, a set of chips. from-scale is how small each starts, from-spread how far along its own spoke it starts as a fraction of the full distance (1 means it does not travel, only grows), and beats how many springs the whole arrival lasts. The gap between one and the next is motion.stagger-ms, shared with every other staggered thing in the app.

motion._comment: Plain numbers, so a CSS duration is built as calc(var(--motion-base-ms) * 1ms). scale is the switch for the ambient loops (the pen bobbing, the mic grille, the mic ring, the shimmer): their choreography keeps its own tempo, multiplied by this, so the Animations setting can stop them all by driving it to 0.
motion._glide_comment: How many screens away a scroll may glide; further jumps go straight there, since a long smooth scroll stops partway (Go to # in a 300-hadith book landed 9,600px short).
motion._hold_comment: A link to one card keeps it at the top while what is above it is still arriving (names, folds), until the reader scrolls or touches, or hold-ms passes. Without it a deep link to Muslim 2927 left the card 4,000px below the screen.
motion._arrive_comment: What a tap brings in is already there on its first frame: arrivals start at this opacity, never 0, so motion polishes the change rather than holding it back. With 0 a new tab or answer read as nothing for most of base-ms, the lag felt on every tap.
motion._reveal_comment: The .reveal class in styles/motion.css: a thing below the fold rises (the rise-in move) and fades in once, when it scrolls into view. reveal-y-px is how far it rises from, reveal-from the opacity it starts at (it is off screen, so unlike arrive-from it may start at 0), reveal-cap how many neighbours in a row stagger before the rest arrive together (--i beyond it counts as the cap, times stagger-ms), so a long grid never makes the last tile wait a second.
motion._tilt_comment: The .tilt class: a card leans toward the pointer on a mouse hover, never on touch. max-deg is the most it leans, perspective-px how far the viewer is from it (smaller is more dramatic).
motion._shake_comment: How long a wrong answer shakes its head. The .shake class in styles/motion.css lasts this long, and the code that clears a shaking tile after it waits this long too, so the two cannot drift apart.
motion._key_hint_comment: How long Home's key hint rests on each tab before it hops to the next (components/shell/KeyHint.jsx).
motion._boot_comment: Opening the app from the home screen: the phone shows its splash (the manifest's dark ground), then the page. There is no tap to answer, so unlike arrive-from the page starts from boot-from and takes boot-ms: a cut from splash to a full screen of text read as a flash. The ground eases from the splash's dark to the chosen look in the same time, so Parchment does not switch on like a light. Drawn by vite/bootShell.js before any script; a device asking for reduced motion gets the cut.
motion._loop_comment: One lap of a slow ambient loop that has no tempo of its own to keep (the mic ring, the Grow ring pulse); a bob is a fraction of it.
motion._enter_comment: A longer arrival than base-ms: a chart rising in, a world tile, the XP bar filling. Celebrations run at twice this.
motion._ease_comment: The one curve the shared moves ride (the Map's rise and hover lifts). slide-ease and settle-ease are the other two named curves.
motion._settle_comment: The curve for anything with weight: a box growing, a block of content arriving, the backdrop drifting. It eases out and stops, where spring-ease overshoots by a tenth; an overshoot suits a small thing landing (a star, the launcher ring) and makes a wide box or a column of text wobble.
motion._slide_comment: A step sideways: the next page, or a strip arriving from the edge, and the same step back as it leaves. slide-px is how far it travels, slide-ease how it settles.
motion._nudge_comment: nudge-px is how far a thing leans under the pointer, a hint it is live rather than a move: a word meaning in the Quran reader (styles/components.css .gloss-all).
motion._patience_comment: Not an animation: how a wait is announced. Nothing is said for the first patience-ms, because an answer that arrives sooner than that has arrived at once as far as the eye is concerned, and a spinner shown and taken away inside a fifth of a second reads as a flash rather than as news. Once something has been said it stays for patience-hold-ms, so an answer landing just after the wait was announced does not snatch it away again. Read in JavaScript by lib/useSlowPending.js, not by the stylesheet, so the Animations setting leaves it alone.

landing._comment: The welcome page's one vertical rhythm: the top and bottom breathing room of every section (hero, manuscript band, tools, finale). Fluid between 64px on a phone and 112px on a wide screen. Change it here and every section moves together.
landing._band_comment: The slim strips between big sections (the trusted-sources banner, the understand band). Small on purpose, so the strip sits snug against the section above and below it instead of floating in space.
landing._gutter_comment: The side margin every landing section shares, so text and cards line up down the whole page instead of each section picking its own.
landing._paper_comment: The parchment band (the understand section) is always paper, in every look: paper is its ground, paper-text and paper-muted its ink, paper-gold the gold deep enough to read on it. The Parchment look is lighter than this on purpose, since whole screens of text sit on it.
landing._size_comment: Fixed sizes that used to sit in the stylesheet. strip-w and strip-h are one tool card in the scroll strip.
landing._phone_comment: Phone only. strip-w-sm and strip-aspect size a tool card in the strip on a phone: nearly the screen wide, and the same shape as the recordings (16 by 10) so the whole screen shows instead of a cropped slice.
landing._hero_comment: The hero keeps its own, smaller top and bottom room instead of section-pad. hero-h is how tall it is: a whole screen on a short one, but never taller than the diagram needs, so a big monitor does not stretch it into empty space (hero-h-sm on a phone, where the copy sits above the diagram and wants the whole screen). hero-title is the headline, sized to stand level with the diagram beside it (hero-title-sm on a phone).
landing._story_comment: The scroll story: four demo steps on one centred stage. story-track-h is how much scrolling the whole story takes (about a screen per step), story-col-w the width of the column, story-stage-h the least height of the stage, which grows to fit its tallest panel (story-stage-h-sm on a phone). story-panel-bg is the dark glass each demo sits on, story-panel-r its corner. step-dim is how faint the steps not yet reached are in the pill row. star-size is the turning geometric star behind the stage, star-lap how long one full steady turn takes, star-opacity how strong its lines are. wave-ms is one swell of the recitation waveform, wave-bars how many bars it has, cap-w the widest a caption gets.
landing._root_comment: The Trace-any-root step. root-parallax-x and root-parallax-y are how many pixels the three big letters drift toward the cursor per depth layer (1 to 3, so the furthest letter moves three times this). orbit-rx is the widest the ring of words around the letters gets, orbit-ry its height, both in pixels (the ring squeezes into a grid under 560px wide). ring-size is how big the tap ripple grows, ring-ms how long it takes.
landing._pan_comment: The See-who-governs step. pan-word is the size of each word on the one-line sentence that slides under the arrows, pan-gap the space between words, pan-dim how faint the words outside the active pair are, pan-tick-w the width of one tick in the strip under it, pan-fade how much of each edge fades out.
landing._finale_comment: The closing section. finale-mark-size is the outlined Tafheem wordmark, finale-rise is how many pixels the wordmark climbs while the section scrolls in.
landing._understand_comment: The 'Are you ready to understand?' band: its letters start scattered and settle as it scrolls up, with three gold rings orbiting behind. understand-rings is the rings' size, understand-scatter how many pixels a letter can start from its place, understand-blur how blurred (px) a fully scattered letter is, understand-spin the seconds the quickest ring takes per turn (the others take a third and two thirds longer), understand-tilt the most the rings lean toward the pointer, in degrees.

layout._comment: How wide the page is allowed to get. Everything down the middle of the app reads this one number through the .shell class, so the header, the tab strip, the banner and the panels can never disagree about where the edges are. It is a maximum, not a width: on any screen narrower than this the page simply fills it, which is what keeps the phone view working.
layout._control_comment: One square for every small control in the page chrome: the settings gear, the pen that opens the launcher, and the height of the command bar between them. One number, so the two ends of the header can never disagree about how tall the row is.
layout._chip_comment: How tall a chip stands, whatever is written in it. Said here rather than left to the text because a pill that takes its height from its own letters is a different height in Arabic than in English: a Recent row holding both came out with the Arabic pills at exactly twice the height of the English ones, a ragged row that looked like a browser bug and was not.
layout._tap_comment: The least height a pill or link stands on a touch screen, where a finger needs more than a pointer does. styles/text.css applies it to .tap when the pointer is coarse; a mouse keeps the compact sizes.
layout._pointer_tap_comment: The least height of a .tap pill or link under a mouse: WCAG 2.5.8's 24px, so a one-line link in a list is never a sliver to aim at. Touch screens get layout.tap instead.
layout._pane_comment: How tall the Quran reader's two panes stand, the surah and the ayah being studied. Each scrolls on its own inside it, so the header, the ayat rail and the recitation bar never leave the screen.
layout._split_comment: How tall the reader stands on a phone while an ayah is studied: the surah over the study, sharing it. Brought up under the top bar, it ends where the recitation bar and the tab bar begin.
layout._nav_comment: How tall the phone's tab bar stands, above the home indicator. The bar is drawn at exactly this and everything that sits clear of it reads the same number: the room kept under the page, the recitation bar resting on it, the reader's split. Left to its own contents the bar came out a few pixels short of the room kept for it, and the page showed through the slit.
layout._tap_min_comment: The least side of anything a finger presses, in px: WCAG 2.5.8 asks 24, Apple's guidelines 44, and 44 is what a thumb hits without aiming. A control that looks smaller keeps its glyph small and gets the rest as padding, so the target grows and the look does not.
layout._proof_comment: The least width of the Nahw full table's proof column on a wide screen, so a rule and its book path read as lines, not a word to a line. A phone sets the proof on its own line under the row instead.
layout._terms_tree_comment: The least page width, in px, at which the hadith Terms view draws the whole tree (components/hadith/TermsView). A floor only: the tree's own width at its smallest legible scale (lib/termsChart wholeWidth) raises it, and below it a phone or tablet gets the groups as a list.
layout._rail_comment: How wide Home's progress column stands beside the tiles on a wide screen (components/home/StatsRail).

sheet._comment: How big a pop-up may get on a wide screen. Maximums, not widths: a phone stays full width. narrow is a short list of choices (settings, a Grow step), standard a pop-up with reading in it (the chain, a phrase, the word bank), wide a pop-up laid out in columns (the sections menu). tall is how much of the screen height any of them may take. narrator is the widest a name box grows in the chain drawing before it wraps.

radius._pill_comment: Fully round ends: the call to action (.cta) and every PrimaryButton. control is the header's chrome (the gear, the pen, the command bar), round like the landing page's; set it to a radius above to square them again.

shadow._comment: Depth, for the few things that float over the page rather than sit in it. pop is a tooltip or popover, lift a card raised under the pointer, scrim the dim behind a modal. One of each, on purpose: one lift reads as one layer.
shadow._elevation_comment: Resting depth, three rungs (styles/motion.css .e1 .e2 .e3): e1 a card on the page, e2 a panel over it (a sheet, a dialog), e3 the top of the stack. Each is a close shadow and a wide soft one, plus a 1px inner highlight along the top edge (edge) that catches the light. pop and lift above stay for what floats or is picked up.

arabic._comment: One ladder for every piece of Arabic in the app, in rem. Smallest first; tiny, small, reading and display are ui/ArabicText's sizes: tiny is a name inside another name; small is a term or a table cell, and a name inside another name in the tarkeeb chart; term is a name read under its word in the chart; reading is Arabic being read: an ayah, a memorise page, a dictionary entry, chart is the sentence the tarkeeb chart is drawn under, read across a row of names rather than as a line; display is a word on its own, in a search box or as an answer; stage is the Arabic a whole page is built around, the words of the landing hero diagram, which have to stand clear of the names under them. The diagram used to keep a ladder of its own, and then a rung of its own, and both times its words drifted a third bigger than the same sentence in the word cards under it. Anything Arabic picks a rung here; nothing sets a size of its own.
arabic._chart_fit_comment: How far the tarkeeb chart may shrink, all of it at once, to fit its box: a long sentence is read whole at a glance rather than a third at a time. Below this the names under the words stop being readable on a phone, so a chart that still does not fit scrolls sideways from here.
arabic._chart_rows_comment: How many rows of names the tarkeeb chart shows before the rest fold behind "more rows": every book example fits in four; a long ayah's widest joins wait for a tap.

mushaf._comment: The Qur'an reader's page view (components/quran/MushafPage). A printed line is drawn as one row and keeps the print's words, so each page sets one font size: the largest at which its longest line still fits. measure-px is the size a line is measured at, gap-em the room between words, fill how much of the width a line spreads across (a short line on the framed first two pages sits in the middle, at centred-fill), page the widest a page stands.

urdu._comment: Urdu rides the Arabic ladder above; only what genuinely differs is here. Nastaliq slopes each word down to the left, so a line needs far more room under it than Naskh does, and two lines set at the Arabic height overlap. Raise this if descenders touch the line below; styles/text.css swaps it in wherever lang="ur".

hadith._comment: The words of a hadith. lines is how much of one hadith shows before the rest waits behind Show the rest.
hadith._way_comment: The chain drawing colours the word between two narrators by how it was received: heard (سمعت، حدّثنا، أخبرنا) and loose (عن, which does not say how). The chain words guide wears the same two.
hadith._chain_comment: chain is the chain of narrators and the English's "Narrated X:" line, read past rather than read: text-faint mixed toward the card, 4.8 to 5.4:1 on the looks (the theme's floor is 4.8), where text-faint alone (6.5 to 7.2:1) sat too near the words it carries.
hadith._weak_comment: The edge and rank numeral on a narrator in the chain drawing, and the filled step on a weak point's scale. One colour for every weak narrator: how weak is said by the rank and the words beside it, never by a shade.

type._comment: English text sizes. In rem, so a browser's own text setting still moves them; px would ignore it. micro/tiny/small are supporting labels, badges, captions, the note under a control. body is English being read rather than labelled: an ayah's translation, a verse's gloss. A translation set at a label size is the mistake this token exists to stop, so reach for body whenever the English is the content.
type._figure_comment: A number read at a glance rather than in a sentence: the three counts on the quiz panel's shut bar. Larger than body on purpose, it is what the row exists to show and it has to win against the words beside it.
type._label_comment: The two rungs the rest of the app is written in: label is a control's own words (a chip, a select, a count) and ui is a line of English inside a control or a card. Tailwind's text-xs and text-sm are pointed at these two in styles/base.css, so every size in the app comes from this file and there is no second scale hiding in the components.
type.label: 0.75rem
type._heading_comment: Headings, smallest to largest: a sheet title (lead), a card or section heading (heading), a tab title (title), a quiz prompt (display). Tailwind's text-base to text-3xl point here.
type.heading: 1.125rem
type.title: 1.25rem

_tarkeeb_comment: The diagram has no sizes of its own any more. Its sentence is the arabic 'chart' rung, its role names 'term', a name inside another name 'small', and its + signs the English type 'body' size. Depth still reads as size, the steps are just shared with the rest of the app instead of being a second private ladder. Its colours are the 'role' group.

pbs._comment: The Map's science charts (lib/pbsData, shell/PbsChart): each branch's own hue, toned per look like the palette so its lines read on every ground. A box is a wash of its hue over the card, head-wash for a branch and wash for a topic, under the look's own text, so nothing pale glares on a dark look.

themes._comment: The looks a reader can pick, and everything the code knows about them: it names none. base is the look the groups above describe. Each entry in looks has a label (what Settings calls it), a scheme (which the browser's own controls, scrollbars and inputs, should match) and then only what it changes, group by group and key by key; the rest stays as above. A new look is mostly its ground and text in color plus a tone: the palette, which tab, role, unit and science all point at, is toned for it, so the sections keep their colours without being listed again. Adding a look is adding an entry here and nothing else: Settings lists it, the page paints its ground before any script runs, and the tests hold it to contrast. device is the reader's "follow my phone or computer" choice: its id and label, and which look a light device and a dark one each get. hint-key is the one localStorage entry that lets the page paint the right ground early (vite/bootShell.js reads it).
themes._tone_comment: How a look tones the palette (lib/tone.js); each look may override any key. centre is where an average colour's OKLCH lightness lands and spread how much of each colour's own lightness difference it keeps (negative on a light look: what is brighter on dark is the emphasis, and emphasis on paper is darker). max-chroma and max-lightness cap it; then it steps away from the ground until min-contrast holds on the page, a card and a raised card. centre 0.8 keeps the dimmest colour near APCA Lc 60, the floor for small text on dark.
themes._comfort_comment: What keeps a look easy on the eyes, by scheme; the tests hold every look to its scheme's limits. Text: no more than text-max-contrast against the brightest ground. On dark (APCA's author) text past Lc 90 glares, and near-white on near-black halates (letters bleed); 12:1 keeps body text comfortable for long reading. On light (British Dyslexia Association) white is too dazzling and black text too stark: cream grounds no lighter than max-ground-lightness, warm dark-brown text at 12.5:1 or less (about Lc 92). dim-min-lc is the APCA Lc floor for secondary text (text-dim) on every ground: WCAG 7.8:1 can still be Lc 54, faint at body size, and 60 is APCA's floor for it. Colour: OKLCH chroma at or under max-chroma; on dark (Material) saturated colours vibrate, Material's 200 tones sit near 0.1; on light they glare less, so the cap is looser. Dark colours are no lighter than max-lightness, so none outshines the text. These are the limits; each look's tone (above) is the recipe, and the tests hold every tone inside them.

dark.label: Midnight
dark._comment: The blue-black look the app wore before Ink: only the ground, text and accent differ.

parchment.label: Parchment
parchment._comment: Ink's light twin: the landing page's warm paper as cream grounds (white dazzles), warm dark-brown text, its palette toned darker by its tone below so each colour reads as text and as a border on the cream (4.5:1 or better); lights stain the ground (multiply) instead of glowing on it. A glow round a word is a light source, which paper has none of: kept to a trace, since at the dark look's strength it blurred the ink and haloed every card.
parchment._tone_comment: Paper tones the palette darker and keeps a little more colour (light grounds glare less). Its one exception: a dark yellow cannot stay yellow (it turns olive-brown), so amber would land on gold; Dictionary's amber leans to orange-brown here to stay its own.

glow._comment: The halo of the .glow box and the .text-glow word (styles/components.css), in the colour of the --c it sits under: a word's role, the chosen tab's line. strength scales both, blur is how far they spread.

font._comment: The landing page's two display faces, now the app's too. head sets page and section titles (h1, h2), label the small capitals over a block (.eyebrow), spaced by label-tracking. Both are bundled (styles/base.css imports them), so no network request blocks a title.
font.head: 'Fraunces Variable', Georgia, serif
font.label: 'Syne', sans-serif

mark._comment: A tab's picture (components/ui/Emblem.jsx). size is the small mark where only a mark fits: the phone's bar, the dock editor, the search rail and rows, the launcher ring (TabMark). head is the picture before a panel's title (SectionHeader), a little taller than the title's capitals so it reads as the title's own.
mark.head: 2.125rem

cta._comment: The call to action (.cta in styles/components.css: Log in, PrimaryButton). pad is its side room, lift-px how far it rises under the pointer and press how small it gives under the finger, nudge-px how far its arrow leans. sheen is how bright the light passing across it is and sheen-beats how long one pass and its rest take, in spring-ms. quiet is the unfilled pill in the header: its height, side room, and the gold of its edge and its hover wash.

tile._comment: A tab's tile on Home (ui/Tile, .tile-wash): under the pointer its Arabic name grows by hover-scale and leans by hover-turn, and the colour wash in its corner deepens from wash to wash-hover.
